text: Learning Rust is worth it. It teaches memory ownership, a concept that makes you a better programmer in every language, because you learn to reason about who owns data and when it is freed. Its compiler catches whole classes of bugs before the program runs, so the effort spent learning pays back in fewer production failures. The question is whether to learn it, not whether to rewrite everything in it, and as a skill it has lasting value.

Learning Rust is not worth it for most people. Its ownership rules and borrow checker make the learning curve steep, so weeks go into fighting the compiler instead of building things. Most jobs ask for Python, JavaScript or Java, so the time has a better return elsewhere. The memory lessons Aegis praises can be learned more cheaply in C or by reading about them. Without a concrete project that needs Rust, the effort buys little.
